item.text: {"search_note":"I found no reliable 2024 evidence that Kishida personally blocked probes into his assets, family, or close associates.\nThe evidence base is strongest for campaign-finance scrutiny and weakest for direct asset/conflict-of-interest investigation.\nThe negative side is therefore structural rather than personal: factional money politics, press-club access limits, and a still-imperfect accountability system.","evidence":[{"title":"Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"January 4, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/04kaiken2.html","summary":"Kishida said the LDP would cooperate with prosecutors, launched a Political Reform Headquarters, and invited external experts to design transparency rules for political funds. This is strong evidence that he tolerated outside scrutiny rather than trying to shut it down.","question_ids":["7B.6","7B.4","7B.5"]},{"title":"Embattled Japan PM faces ethics committee, with popularity and budget on the line","publisher":"Reuters","date":"February 28, 2024","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/economy/embattled-japan-pm-faces-ethics-committee-to-save-popularity-and-budget-3319362","summary":"Kishida became the first sitting Japanese prime minister to appear before a parliamentary ethics committee over the funding scandal, showing that independent legislative scrutiny of his conduct was real and publicly sustained.","question_ids":["7B.6","7B.4"]},{"title":"Prosecutors make first arrest in political funding scandal","publisher":"Reuters","date":"January 7, 2024","url":"https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Japan-prosecutors-make-first-arrest-in-political-funding-scandal-45687976/","summary":"Prosecutors arrested a ruling-party lawmaker over alleged fundraising kickbacks and off-book money. This is negative evidence that the environment around Kishida involved real independent investigation of political finance, not a sealed system.","question_ids":["7B.6","7B.4"]},{"title":"Prosecutors indict several LDP faction members over funds scandal","publisher":"Kyodo News","date":"January 19, 2024","url":"https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2024/01/f4d6ea5b7d8f-update1-prosecutors-indict-several-ldp-faction-members-over-funds-scandal.html","summary":"Prosecutors indicted multiple ruling-party faction figures, including a former accountant from Kishida’s group, over undisclosed revenue in a slush-fund scandal. This is the clearest sign that independent investigation reached Kishida’s factional orbit.","question_ids":["7B.6","7B.4","7B.5"]},{"title":"Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"June 21, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202406/21kaiken.html","summary":"Kishida said disclosure thresholds were lowered and that a third-party body for inspections and audits should be created. This is direct evidence that he supported independent oversight mechanisms rather than insulating political money from review.","question_ids":["7B.6","7B.4"]},{"title":"Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"August 14, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202408/14kaiken.html","summary":"Kishida said the LDP presidential race should be transparent, with free and vigorous debate, and that he would step aside and support the successor chosen by vote. This supports a broader reading that he did not resist accountability or independent contestation.","question_ids":["7B.6","7B.3","7B.5"]},{"title":"Japan: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/japan/freedom-world/2024","summary":"Freedom House says Japan generally operates with openness and transparency, but officials sometimes withheld information in scandal contexts and press-club structures still constrain access. This is mixed evidence: independent investigation exists, but informational friction remains.","question_ids":["7B.6"]},{"title":"Japan: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/japan/freedom-net/2024","summary":"Freedom House says government pressure and the kisha kurabu system contribute to self-censorship and restricted access for some journalists and outlets. This is negative structural evidence against fully robust independent investigation, even though it is not Kishida-specific repression.","question_ids":["7B.6"]},{"title":"World Report 2024: Japan","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/japan","summary":"HRW said Japan’s “hostage justice” system still involved coercive questioning, repeated arrests, denial of bail, and weak legal access. This undercuts any claim that Kishida had built a fully strong ecosystem for independent scrutiny and correction.","question_ids":["7B.6"]}]}
